title: Sensory Perception Mechanism for Preparing the Combinations of Stimuli Operation in the Architectural Experience
research_question: To clarify the sensory perception mechanism for sensory stimuli operation in architectural experience, specifically: (1) to identify comparative sensitive domains and differences in sensitivity among various sensory stimuli in a wooden micro-architectural space; and (2) to examine the effects of dynamic changes of a single stimulus (dynamically coloured light) on participants' perceptions and emotions.

participants.description: Experiment 1: 72 college-aged male and female students (mean age 20.5 years, range 20-22) from China, well-educated, no related perception disease, rested and calm. 60 acceptable responses (30 female, 30 male). Experiment 2: 107 college-aged male and female students (mean age 22.4 years, range 18-23) from China, no visual perception disease, energetic and no severe emotional fluctuations. 90 acceptable responses (45 female, 45 male).
participants.recruitment: Participated in the experiment on campus.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: A wooden micro building (2.2m L x 2.0m W x 2.3m H) with basic furniture, upholstered items with curved volumetric geometries, unique smells, and music. Sensory stimuli included: visual (colours of wall/ceiling/furniture, decorative pattern, individual ornaments, volumetric geometry), auditory (music), olfactory (smell), tactile (texture of wall/furniture), kinaesthesia (elasticity of floor).

A paper architectural model (2m L x 2m W x 1m H) with three rooms, a balcony, basic furniture and ornaments. Ten kinds of dynamically coloured lights were projected into the model: red, orange, yellow, chartreuse, green, cyan, blue, purple, purplish-red, and white.

measures.instrument: Five-point Likert scale (-2 'strongly disagree' to +2 'strongly agree')
Five-point Likert scale (-2 'strongly disagree' to +2 'strongly agree')
In-depth interview questions about feelings (e.g., anxiety, romantic, happy, calm, sad)

mechanisms: People are used to obtaining most information from visual senses directly and conveniently.
Ambient odours have repeatedly proven to be able to influence both mood and behaviour in people.
Auditory modalities significantly contribute to a more comprehensive perception and evaluation of indoor environments.
Kinaesthesia domain has a close relationship with human behaviour and may not be perceived directly.
Colour can be more easily perceived than decorative patterns and individual ornaments are used to attract attention.
Architectural space can have a diverse emotional significance and impact on an individual's emotional state.
Cultural background influences colour preference (e.g., white in Asian regions).
The notion of congruency and superadditivity can enhance perception.
moderators: Cultural background (e.g., Asian regions for white color preference)
implementation_implications: The study provides a theoretical foundation for sensory choice, sensory perception enhancement, and the combination forms of sensory perceptions.
Perception design of overlapped multi-sensory stimuli and single dynamic stimuli can improve indoor environment quality in normal and intelligent multi-sensory architecture.
Sensory stimuli and domains with higher sensitivity levels should receive more attention for perception enhancement.
Dynamically coloured light can play an important role in interactive perception design due to its quick feedback and significant effect on participants' preferences and emotions.
Yellow light, purplish-red, cyan, and orange are favorable choices for perception design to improve human behaviors and indoor environment quality.
Bright curtains or walls (visual domain with highest sensitivity) and the scent of flowers (olfactory domain with second-highest sensitivity) can cheer up a dull room.

limitations: The first experiment was confined to Chinese culture to avoid the impacts of different cultures.
The participant pool consisted solely of young adults (college students), which may limit generalizability to other age groups or populations.

crossref_abstract: Sensory stimuli in an architectural space play an important role in the human perception of the indoor environment, no matter whether they are static or dynamic, isolated, or combined. By enhancing some perceptions in the sensory stimuli, the overall perceptions of an architectural space can be improved, especially for an intelligent architectural space. As yet, there are few studies reported about the sensory perception mechanism for the sensory stimuli operation in the architectural experience. In this research, a wooden micro building was prepared for the study of the sensitivity level of participants to various sensory stimuli in the same and in different sensory domains. Participants’ visual, auditory, olfactory, tactile and kinaesthesia perceptions were discussed statistically in terms of the sensitivity level. Based on the study, the effect of a single dynamic sensory stimulus (a dynamically coloured light) on the participants’ perception was studied in a paper architectural model from two aspects including preference and emotion. The dynamically coloured light was discussed statistically in terms of the level of preference. The study showed that there are significant differences among participants’ levels of sensitivity to the different sensory domains and to the different sensory stimuli. In particular, the sensitivity level to the stimulus that is the colour of a space is the highest of all stimuli. As a single changing sensory stimulus, a dynamically coloured light can lead to significant mood fluctuations and changes in the preference level. In particular, yellow is the favourite colour of light. The object of this study is expected to provide a theoretical foundation that is related to sensory choice, sensory perception enhancement and the combination forms of sensory perceptions. Based on the theoretical foundation, the perception design of overlapped multi-sensory stimuli and a single dynamic stimulus can be conducted to improve the quality of the indoor environment of normal and intelligent multi-sensory architecture.
